rationale: bugs_open/280: check_decision_guards.go's storedPageAssemblySQL (the single, deliberately-shared definition of "the page, as stored" used both by the check and its own completion verifier, VerifyDecisionRegressionResolved) reads pg.rendered_header/pg.rendered_footer to build the document every decision guard is evaluated against. Those two columns are the same vestigial pages.rendered_header/footer/head columns bugs_open/270 documents as empty on all 694 pages fleet-wide -- chrome is written to site_components by render_site_components, not back onto the pages row, and has not been for some time. So the 'stored assembly' this check evaluates every guard against silently omits all chrome, always: a contains guard asserting something lives in the header or footer would ALWAYS report a violation (false positive -- the decision reads as broken when it isn't); a not_contains guard on chrome/nav content would ALWAYS report clean (false negative -- a real regression in the header/footer would never be caught). No wrong verdict has been observed yet: all 5 live doc_notes rows with categories ? 'decision-record' were read in full (cheap at this count, not sampled) and none currently assert anything about header/footer/nav content. This is the silent-but-real, no-symptom-yet case the standing debugging guide asks to be filed and fixed before the first chrome-scoped decision discovers it the hard way -- and the mechanism, evidence and false-premise checks are documented in bugs_open/280 itself, substituting first-hand verification for the 090 diagnosis loop per the 2026-07-31 ruling (the mechanism is seven lines of quoted SQL read directly from the file; the vestigial-columns premise is the same fleet-wide measurement already established for bugs_open/270 and re-confirmed live the same day). This submission fixes it the same way 270 fixed the sibling defect in a different check: retype the shared SQL constant to read chrome from site_components. Full design reasoning: docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_280_decision_guards_chrome/PLAN_2026-08-16_decision_guards_chrome.md.

plan.summary: Retype check_decision_guards.go's storedPageAssemblySQL constant to read the site's header and footer slots from site_components (site-scoped, since chrome is shared across a site's pages, not page-scoped) ahead of the existing page_components aggregation for the named page. The FROM pages pg WHERE pg.site_id = $1 AND pg.name = $2 gate stays unchanged -- it is what makes the query return zero rows when the named page does not exist, which both the check (skip, not this check's finding) and the verifier (fail-closed error, RFC_017) rely on to tell 'page missing' apart from 'page exists with empty chrome'. Because the check and verifier already share this one constant by design ('so the two cannot drift', per the file's own comment), one fix covers both call sites. Add a test file asserting on the actual SQL text issued, plus two behavioural tests demonstrating the fix closes both the false-positive and false-negative shapes described above.

edits.rationale: This one constant is the entire defect -- both the check's Run and VerifyDecisionRegressionResolved evaluate every guard against whatever it produces, and today that is chrome-free by construction.
edits.sketch: Replace `SELECT COALESCE(pg.rendered_header,'') || COALESCE(pg.rendered_footer,'') || COALESCE((SELECT string_agg(...) FROM page_components pc WHERE pc.page_id = pg.id), '') FROM pages pg WHERE pg.site_id = $1 AND pg.name = $2` with `SELECT COALESCE((SELECT sc.rendered_html FROM site_components sc WHERE sc.site_id = $1 AND sc.slot_name = 'header'), '') || COALESCE((SELECT sc.rendered_html FROM site_components sc WHERE sc.site_id = $1 AND sc.slot_name = 'footer'), '') || COALESCE((SELECT string_agg(COALESCE(pc.rendered_html,''), '' ORDER BY pc.position) FROM page_components pc WHERE pc.page_id = pg.id), '') FROM pages pg WHERE pg.site_id = $1 AND pg.name = $2` -- the page_components term and the outer FROM/WHERE are byte-for-byte unchanged; only the header/footer terms move from pg.rendered_* to correlated site_components scalar subqueries keyed on $1 (site_components has a UNIQUE(site_id, slot_name) constraint, confirmed via \d site_components, so a scalar SELECT per slot is correct without string_agg).

edits.rationale: A happy-path sqlmock test would stay green even if the query silently reverted to pg.rendered_header/footer, since sqlmock returns whatever row a test hands it regardless of the WHERE/SELECT clause actually issued -- check_missing_structure_test.go in the same package already establishes the pattern for guarding against exactly this class of regression.
edits.sketch: Three tests: (1) TestDecisionGuardsAssemblyReadsSiteComponents asserts the storedPageAssemblySQL constant's text mentions site_components for both header and footer slots, still reads page_components for the body, still gates on FROM pages pg WHERE pg.site_id=$1 AND pg.name=$2, and never again mentions pg.rendered_(header|footer); (2) TestDecisionGuardsContainsGuardSeesChromeContent feeds Run() a mocked assembled string that carries a pattern only in the header and asserts a contains guard on that pattern does NOT fire; (3) TestDecisionGuardsNotContainsGuardCatchesChromeRegression feeds a mocked assembled string carrying chrome content and asserts a not_contains guard on that content DOES fire. Mutation-tested: reverted the constant to the pre-fix SQL locally, confirmed test (1) -- and only test (1) -- fails, then restored the fix; full package suite and `go build ./...` both green afterward.

grounded_in: check_decision_guards.go:72-78 (pre-fix): `SELECT COALESCE(pg.rendered_header,'') || COALESCE(pg.rendered_footer,'') || COALESCE((SELECT string_agg(COALESCE(pc.rendered_html,''), '' ORDER BY pc.position) FROM page_components pc WHERE pc.page_id = pg.id), '') FROM pages pg WHERE pg.site_id = $1 AND pg.name = $2`

Confirms site_components.slot_name IS the plain vocabulary ('header'/'footer'/'head'); content_components.function is a DIFFERENT table's DIFFERENT column, used only to resolve which library component definition serves a slot. This fix reads site_components.rendered_html by slot_name directly and never touches content_components or this resolver -- the resolver exists, it is simply not on this fix's code path.

ROUND 1 REVISE CORRECTION -- the decision-record row count has moved since 280 was filed: `SELECT count(*) FROM doc_notes WHERE categories ? 'decision-record';` now returns 8, not 5 (3 new rows landed 2026-08-15 same-day, from the unrelated bugs_open/279 workstream). Row count is the wrong denominator, though: DecisionGuardsCheck.Run() skips any row with no parseable ```guard fence. `SELECT subject_key, (body LIKE '%```guard%') FROM doc_notes WHERE categories ? 'decision-record' ORDER BY created_at;` shows only 2 of 8 have one -- D-001-free-beside-paid and D-002-no-tools-directory-on-index. Read both in full: D-001 asserts an href inside the page-body brief-explanation slot; D-002's own decision text explicitly scopes itself to 'no section OUTSIDE header/footer', i.e. deliberately excludes chrome. So exactly 2 live enforceable guards exist today, both page-body-scoped by their own stated design -- a stronger, more precise version of the original 'currently symptom-free' claim, not a weaker one.
plan.risks: The FROM pages pg WHERE pg.site_id = $1 AND pg.name = $2 gate is deliberately kept unchanged rather than simplified, specifically to avoid a bare `SELECT <subqueries>` with no FROM clause -- that shape always returns exactly one row, which would silently break the 'missing page yields zero rows' contract both the check (skip as not-this-check's-finding) and the fail-closed verifier (RFC_017: a missing page must error, not resolve) depend on. A reviewer should confirm this reasoning holds -- i.e. that the fixed query still returns zero rows, not a row with empty-string chrome, when dctx.SiteID/p.guard.Page names a page that does not exist. Second: this changes what VerifyDecisionRegressionResolved evaluates too (the two call sites share the one constant by design), so a decision-record guard that was previously evaluated as always-passing (a contains guard someone wrote, not realising it could never fail because chrome was never included) could start reporting decision_regression items once this ships -- the corrected live census (see grounded_in) found exactly 2 enforceable guards exist today and both are page-body-scoped by their own stated design, but a reviewer with visibility into decision-record authoring practice elsewhere should double check nothing relies on the current (broken) always-pass behaviour. Third, ROUND 1 addition: site_components.slot_name vocabulary is now verified live (header/footer/head, 22/22/22, no other values) and cross-checked against ChromeSlotFunction's doc comment in component_library.go, which confirms slot_name and content_components.function are deliberately different vocabularies for different purposes and this fix is on the slot_name side throughout -- a reviewer should confirm no other live code path writes a different slot_name value to site_components for header/footer (none found; grep for `slot_name` assignments across the codebase turns up only the two ChromeSlotFunction-mediated writers, both using the plain vocabulary).
